question.problem:
The function $f(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{log}_{5}⁡(2x+k), & x\ne -1, \\ 3, & x=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=-1,$ what is the value of $k?$

$k=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
From the definition of $f(x),$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -1}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to -1}{log}_{5}⁡(2x+k) \\  & ={log}_{5}⁡(k-2).\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x=-1,$ we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -1}f(x) & =f(-1) \\ {log}_{5}⁡(k-2) & =3 \\ k-2 & ={5}^{3} \\ k-2 & =125 \\ k & =127.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, setting $k=127$ removes the point discontinuity.
